decisions.reason: Text-internal and editorially standard: does the conceit keep paying out after its reveal. Negative sign plausibly reflects community appetite for punchline flash fiction, not a defect.
Conflict among feeling, belief, and behavior is canonical evidence of characterization depth. Low anchor slightly bundles 'obvious' with 'unsupported', but scoring remains consistent.
Counts presence of formal mimicry, a stylistic habit; its failing anchor explicitly penalizes 'well-made paragraphs'. Absent mimesis is no quality defect, so this belongs on the nuisance side.
As written it counts indirection versus direct statement categorically, not whether meaning lands. Well-executed exposition is penalized, making this a show-don't-tell style habit.
'Most predictable reading' is defined against an unseen distribution of other responses to the same prompt; a judge scoring one story cannot apply it consistently.
